subject: Split KMS proposal, analytics carve-out, and subprocessor roster
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@iona.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Iona Legal <legal@iona.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency + split-key idea / initial DPA redlines attached

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks for the earlier demo — the product looks promising. Legal here (cc'd) has a couple of follow-ups as we get into procurement:

1) We need an explicit residency commitment for customer content (EU primary for our tenant).
2) We are open to a narrow analytics/telemetry carve-out to US for operational telemetry only, but we need retention limits and pseudonymization.
3) We have an idea: could Redwood support a split-KMS model where Iona supplies a customer-managed key (CMK) that encrypts/unwraps the customer content at rest in the EU, while Redwood retains a separate key for telemetry/metrics stored in the US? This would help satisfy our regulators.

I've attached a redline to your standard DPA (iona_dpa_redlines_v2.pdf). Also request a current subprocessor roster and any evidence around short-term cross-region caching windows.

Can we have a short call next week to talk feasibility and any operational caveats (especially for APAC users hitting EU-pinned content)?

Best,
Sara Lopez
Head of Privacy / Iona Therapeutics

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency + split-key idea / initial DPA redlines attached

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear note and for the DPA redline. We're happy to explore the split-KMS approach. High level response below; we can walk through in a call.

Summary of a possible model:
- Customer content pin: We can pin customer content to an EU primary placement and require a customer-managed KMS (supported in Redwood Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we can support BYOK via external KMS in supported clouds). The CMK would be used for envelope encryption of the stored payload in the EU.
- Analytics carve-out: Operational telemetry (latency, token counts, error rates, anonymized traces) can be routed to a US analytics cluster. We would apply pseudonymization: no persistent plaintext content, only event-level metadata. Retention can be limited (proposal below).
- Temporary cross-region caching: For performance we use ephemeral prefix/KV caches that may briefly touch regional edge nodes. We can commit to TTLs (e.g., <6 hours) for any transient caches and log those hops in audit trails.

Open items for legal ops:
- Acceptable retention window for analytics (we propose 72 hours by default, configurable to shorter windows).
- Whether the DPA needs explicit language about CMK custody, key rotation, and split-key obligations.
- Subprocessor roster: sharing attached (redwood_subprocessor_roster_2026-07.csv).

Next steps: Marissa / Kimberly — can you confirm technical constraints and a short internal runbook we can share with Iona? If acceptable, propose a call Thursday 07/15 at 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
Sean
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: viability notes for Iona split-KMS + analytics carve-out

Sean / Kim / Priyom — quick internal note after reviewing the redline and the ask. High-level feasibility and operational guardrails below; I'll convert to a customer-facing runbook if we align: 

Feasibility: doable with caveats.
- BYOK/CMK: Supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted tenants we'll need to provision external KMS access (customer-managed key in EU region). Key wrapping/envelope encryption approach recommended (we don't hold plaintext key material).
- Live inference path: model inference happens in the region where the model is pinned (EU). For APAC users, this increases egress latency; we should surface expected p99 latency delta (rough estimate +60–140ms depending on cloud region).
- KV/prefix cache: Edge caches may hold short-lived KV entries; we must enforce TTL < 6 hours and scrub textual windows for Iona-specific customers.
- Analytics: strongly recommend stripping prompt/response content before any telemetry export. Keep event ids + hashed user id + token counters. Retention: 72 hours by default; legal can request 24 hours.
- Failover: If EU primary becomes unavailable, we can fail over to a geo-compatible EU replica. We should avoid failover to US for customer content unless contract explicitly allows temporary cross-border exceptions.

Action items for the thread: 
1) Priyom — prepare a one-page ops runbook describing CMK provisioning and key rotation steps.
2) Kimberly — legal question: do the redlines require us to escrow keys or provide key material in an emergency? (my read: customer retains control; we need DPA language only).
3) Sean — confirm go/no-go for call and share the ops runbook + roster with Iona after legal sign-off.

I'll attach the internal checklist and the subprocessor CSV export for sharing.

-Marissa
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Data residency + split-key idea / initial DPA redlines attached

Sara / Iona Legal — thanks for your patience; attaching the materials below and summarizing commitments we can make today.

Commitments we can provide now:
- Pinning: Iona tenant content (production payloads) can be pinned to EU primary placement.
- CMK support: We support a customer-managed key model for content encryption in the EU (BYOK). Key rotation and provisioning steps are documented in the attached runbook.
- Analytics carve-out: Operational telemetry will be pseudonymized and routed to a US analytics cluster only. No persistent plaintext customer content will be exported. Proposed default retention = 72 hours (we can agree a shorter window in the DPA).
- Transient caches: Any cross-region caches are ephemeral and TTL-limited (<6 hours). We will log and expose cache hop telemetry in the audit trail.
- Subprocessors: attached current roster; we will notify you 30 days before adding any new processor.

Requested DPA changes: please incorporate BYOK language that clarifies CMK custody and restricts Redwood access. We propose a clause about temporary analytics carve-outs and the 72-hour retention cap.

Next steps: 
1) Iona to review attached runbook + roster and confirm whether 72h retention is acceptable or if you require 24h.
2) If acceptable, Legal to return a clean DPA for signature; we can then schedule a technical onboarding call to provision the CMK and test PKI.

Thanks — attaching: internal_cmkrunbook_draft.pdf, redwood_subprocessor_roster_2026-07.csv, and a short one-page overview.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
